I had this exact same error ("Fatal error in GC: SuspendThread loop failed" on launch). Fix that worked for me: disabling Windows "Memory Integrity" (HVCI) under Windows Security > Device Security > Core Isolation. Restarted the PC and VRChat launched fine right away.

My guess is this is a conflict between Easy Anti-Cheat and HVCI - and since Microsoft is starting to auto-enable Memory Integrity on more Windows 11 PCs via quality updates from October 2026 (announced Sept 1, 2026), more players will likely run into this going forward.

GPU: RTX 5070 Ti, Windows 11.

@{62e04e97eea34044b94f17ec|full_name}

I’ve been seeing reports on X where different things seem to help, such as verifying VRChat’s files on Steam, uninstalling a Windows Update, removing launch options.

However, what works seems to vary from person to person, and there doesn’t seem to be a single fix that works for everyone.

Disabling Memory Integrity didn’t help in my case either.

I hope more reports keep coming in so we can get a better idea of what’s actually causing this issue.
@{6aa3f919b4e14901d07dbee4|full_name} I hope so too. This error is frustateing

i went through the dmp file with WinDbg of a friend that is currently encountering this error. I'm far from knowledgeable in dump file analysis but looking up the stuff that looks interesting, I found that the reported error (at least in 2 samples I looked at) is invalid pointer/error c0000005 where the unity engine dll is trying to read address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF.

(Note: this is different from someone else's report. So honestly this whole comment might not be of any value if I accidentally captured the wrong thing... See note in next paragraph)

Among others, from the dump file:

`FAILURE_BUCKET_ID: INVALID_POINTER_READ_c0000005_UnityPlayer.dll!Unknown`

However, although I can't be sure at all, this doesn't seem to be related to SuspendThread that the error actually shows the user, and c0000005 might just be how Unity is exiting when it encounters that actual bug that I'm not seeing (other than memory issue but seems weird given everyone else's conflicting reports and resolutions). 

Also ran `lm` and no weird DLLs are present in the dump file just to confirm that it doesn't look like this issue is from anything external.

Hope this is of some use to someone maybe, otherwise uh idk. We are in the witchcraft stage of this bug where everyone seems to be saying something different, hopefully it gets narrowed down on.

Also again, for the record, the friend in question tried quite literally everything you could even remotely think of for troubleshooting including some more advanced stuff. At one time, running `sfc /scannow` let them keep the game running and join a populated instance but they still crashed shortly after in a completely empty instance of the vrchat homeworld.

For what's it's worth, if you have razer products, disabling the Razer Cortex overlay fixed it for me. Nothing else i found could fix it, so might be something with EAC flagging it?? No idea just thought id add my experience.
To anyone coming across this thread, Malwarebytes was causing the crash on my end, adding the folder AND the exe to the allow list fixed my problem

Interesting finding, it seems that there are 2 errors.

On a fresh system where the bug happens, the error window about SuspendThread loop failing appears once. Subsequent launches may or may not crash, but will eventually crash on a world change.

My message above is the dump file of one of those subsequent crashes that do NOT show the SuspendThread loop failed window (just a hard crash).

On a dump file that was generated specifically by crashing from SuspendThread, the error changes:

`FAILURE_BUCKET_ID:  BREAKPOINT_80000003_GameAssembly.dll!Unknown`

This is the actual SuspendThread failure I wasn't seeing originally, but my lack of skill means I can't really tell anything beyond this. Very light research just brings me back to the SuspendThread failure within Unity and nothing in the dump file actually supports finding a specific root cause.

With regards to SuspendThread, as far as I can tell once again, it's Unity trying to pause the threads it manages to do a GC pass and something is preventing it. People reporting disabling software that interacts with low-level OS stuff (e.g. anti-virus, HVCI, garbage RGB apps) might indicate that something somewhere updated (VRC, Windows, or anything else that most people have) which changed some behaviour possibly with some DLL related to what Unity is trying to do.

I'm just yapping at this point and I can't really say anything productive beyond everything above but if anyone has an idea or wants me to check something, let me know.

My friend encountering this error has already provided the same dump files I'm looking at to VRC feedback/support (and was told to try using a SteamVR beta when their request clearly said this bug also occurs in desktop mode).

Basic system info if relevant:

- Win11 fully up to date

- Nvidia 4090

- Nvidia Studio Driver 619.92 (i doubt graphic drivers are the cause. If anyone here confirms an AMD GPU also has the issue, or an old NV game ready driver is also causing the issue, the fact the latest studio drivers also have the issue would dispel any suspicion about GPU drivers)

- AMD 7950X3D

If anyone has a drastically different configuration than the above, this could inform which parameter is a likely cause. Personally I'm starting to suspect windows updates or a combination of windows updates and VRC updates. Just speculation, I have absolutely no clue.

If i made any very wrong statements from my own lack of knowledge in the above post, please correct me and I will edit it

verified with my friend if we had different windows updates installed using update history, since I don't have the issue. However, there doesn't seem to be anything different. The updates that happened closely before the issue started and which both my friend and I have installed (for the record) are:

- KB5124008 (26200.9445)

- KB5126052

We also both have all Windows 11 updates prior to those with no divergence.

For the record, my system is as follows and doesn't encounter the issue:

- Win11 fully up to date

- Nvidia 4070ti

- Nvidia Game Ready Driver 616.92

- AMD 5800X3D

If it matters, friend is using Index, I'm using Beyond headset. At this point just trying to look for any correlation or helping others figure something out.

Happened to me yesterday for the first time in awhile (launching both in VR mode and desktop mode).

This seems to come in fits and bouts for me. Will happen consistently for awhile then stop just as randomly. In the past have tried removing USB peripherals (excluding plain keyboard/mouse) and many of the other suggestions out there to no luck.

Same crash, confirmed via crash dump analysis:

- VRChat 2022.3.22.13999, non-VR mode, crashes ~20s after launch (during load)

- Exception: EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT (0x80000003), faulting module GameAssembly.dll, offset 0x0000000000a8a05a

- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D (32 logical processors), OS: Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200.9457)

- Memory Integrity (HVCI) already OFF, Razer Cortex not installed — so those two commonly-suggested fixes don't apply here

- Dump shows ~225 live threads at crash time, so the GC's SuspendThread loop likely times out suspending one of them
